quantity: Median energy per text prompt, production AI assistant
hardware_or_model: Google TPU serving fleet, Gemini Apps text prompts
measurement_method: production instrumentation of full serving stack (active accelerator power + host system + idle machine capacity + data-centre overhead)
caveat: Median, not mean; text prompts only; accounting boundary deliberately includes idle capacity and facility overhead, so NOT comparable to GPU-telemetry-only per-query figures.

quantity: Median water consumption per text prompt
hardware_or_model: Google TPU serving fleet, Gemini Apps text prompts
measurement_method: production instrumentation, same boundary as EQ-01
caveat: Direct on-site water only as framed in the abstract; indirect (electricity-embedded) water not included in this figure.

quantity: Year-on-year reduction in energy per median prompt
caveat: Bundles software efficiency work AND fleet/hardware change; the paired 44x carbon reduction additionally bundles clean-energy procurement. Not a pure efficiency factor.

quantity: Year-on-year reduction in carbon per median prompt
caveat: Includes clean-energy procurement; not attributable to compute efficiency alone.

quantity: Energy per long prompt, most energy-intensive model in survey
hardware_or_model: 30 commercial API models, datacentre hardware statistically inferred
measurement_method: public API performance data x company-specific environmental multipliers; hardware configuration inferred, not observed
caveat: Hardware configuration is inferred rather than measured; 'long prompt' length not fixed across providers. Do not mix with EQ-01.

quantity: Spread between most and least energy-intensive model per long prompt
caveat: Spread conflates model size, provider hardware and provider accounting multipliers.

quantity: Energy per short query (low end of surveyed range)
caveat: ~1.75x the measured Google median (EQ-01) despite being the survey's low end: different accounting boundary and inferred hardware.

quantity: Energy per output token, short-output regime
hardware_or_model: Llama-3.2-1B on NVIDIA H200, batch 16, context 4K, 10 output tokens
caveat: Token energy here is dominated by the fixed prefill + generation-setup cost amortised over only 10 tokens.

quantity: Energy per output token, long-output regime
hardware_or_model: Llama-3.2-1B on NVIDIA H200, batch 16, context 4K, 512 output tokens
caveat: Same request configuration as ET-01: a 10.4x fall in per-token energy while total request energy RISES. Per-token energy alone is not a valid cost metric.

quantity: Total batched inference-window energy, short vs long output
hardware_or_model: Llama-3.2-1B on NVIDIA H200, batch 16, context 4K, 10 vs 512 output tokens
caveat: Pairs with ET-01/ET-02; use as the worked example of the token-energy vs request-energy mismatch.

quantity: Batching gain in per-token energy, batch-16 vs batch-1
hardware_or_model: NVIDIA H100/H200, dense and MoE models, 10 output tokens
caveat: Batching benefit is context-length-bounded; a single batching speedup constant is not defensible across context lengths.

quantity: Energy per output token, small local models
caveat: Consumer hardware, small models, unsaturated serving. Not comparable to datacentre-accelerator figures. Authors label the study preliminary.

quantity: Throughput of most efficient small local models
caveat: Batch size not stated in the retrieved abstract; treat as single-stream throughput until confirmed.

quantity: Per-token energy penalty of a 7B model vs most efficient model in set
hardware_or_model: Mistral-7B vs sub-1.5B models, consumer GPU
caveat: Cross-model, same hardware; does not isolate quantisation or serving-engine effects.

quantity: System energy per output token, sequential agent vs saturated serving
hardware_or_model: 2x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, Qwen3 ~27B class model
measurement_method: full-stack telemetry: NVML GPU counters + Intel RAPL CPU/DRAM + IPMI system sensors
caveat: LARGEST NOT-LIKE-FOR-LIKE HAZARD IN THIS TABLE. Compares an unbatched single-tenant agent loop against a saturated multi-request server; the factor bundles absent batching, inter-turn context growth and tool-induced idle time. It is not a measure of 'agentic overhead' at matched serving conditions.

quantity: Fraction of system energy invisible to GPU-only telemetry
hardware_or_model: 2x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell node, three agent/serving workloads
measurement_method: NVML vs RAPL vs IPMI cross-comparison
caveat: Node-level figure on a 2-GPU workstation-class system; the non-GPU share will differ on dense 8-GPU datacentre nodes. Use as a lower bound on boundary error, not a universal constant.

quantity: Extra output tokens generated by extended-thinking mode
hardware_or_model: Qwen3 ~27B class model, mathematical reasoning datasets
caveat: Range spans datasets; pair with AG-04.

quantity: Difference in per-token energy between thinking and non-thinking modes
caveat: Strong support for modelling reasoning cost as token volume x constant per-token energy, within one model and one serving regime.

quantity: System-level energy-efficiency gain from continuous batching, 1 to 16 req/s
caveat: GPU power plateaus while throughput rises; gain is specific to this node and request-rate range.

quantity: Energy multiplier of multi-agent vs non-agentic baseline, mean
hardware_or_model: multiple agentic LLM configurations on developer workloads, multiple hardware targets
measurement_method: measured energy and runtime comparison across agent designs
caveat: Mean across task-hardware pairs; worst case reported as up to 160x for individual pairs. Task set is developer workflows only.

quantity: Worst-case slowdown of multi-agent design, individual task-hardware pair
caveat: Single worst pair, not a distributional summary; do not use as a central estimate.

quantity: Energy multiplier of agentic workflow vs equivalent single-pass inference
hardware_or_model: generic; scales with number of model and tool calls
measurement_method: order-of-magnitude estimation from published data; authors state no original physical measurement
caveat: Explicitly a conceptual estimate. Useful as a framing bound, unusable as a model parameter.

quantity: Token-consumption multiplier of multi-agent system vs single-agent core
hardware_or_model: LLM multi-agent workflows on HumanEval / IFEval / pooled benchmarks
caveat: Token counts, not energy; accuracy changes are mixed (LLM-Debate +9.67 pts HumanEval but -1.96 pts pooled).

quantity: Share of agent tokens spent on localisation/understanding plus vulnerability reasoning
hardware_or_model: LLM coding agents on vulnerability-detection tasks
measurement_method: per-phase token attribution over agent traces
caveat: Single task domain (vulnerability detection); phase taxonomy is task-specific.

quantity: Agent total-cost reduction from targeted context/phase optimisation
measurement_method: measured token/cost accounting with success-rate control
caveat: 20 tasks only; 'cost' is token/API cost, not joules.

quantity: Token reduction from predictive budget control at matched trace completion
hardware_or_model: agent traces, SWE-bench Verified and 3 other suites, 6 agent models
measurement_method: offline budget-control replay against a fixed-budget policy
caveat: Replay, not live deployment; matched-completion constraint is the authors' own.

quantity: Overhead of in-trajectory token forecasting
unit: ms mean cumulative prediction time per run
caveat: Latency overhead only; no additional LLM calls, so near-zero token overhead.

quantity: Per-GPU power-cap range over which throughput is unaffected
hardware_or_model: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, memory-bandwidth-bound reasoning workload
measurement_method: measured throughput under enforced power caps
caveat: Throughput drops sharply at 300 W. Applies to a memory-bound decode workload; compute-bound prefill will respond differently.

quantity: Decode energy recoverable by clock locking rather than power capping
measurement_method: measured phase-resolved energy under clock-lock vs power-cap control
caveat: Authors report clock locking Pareto-dominates power capping; power capping alone is the weaker lever for decode.

quantity: Error of load-scaled TDP as a power-draw proxy vs learned model
unit: x higher median absolute percentage error
measurement_method: leave-one-GPU-out / leave-one-LLM-out cross-validation against measured power
caveat: Direct evidence that vendor TDP scaled by utilisation is a poor energy-model parameter. Learned model reaches <=3.4% MAPE offline, <=13.5% server, on unseen GPUs.

quantity: Accuracy of compositional power-trace generation for LLM inference
hardware_or_model: multiple LLMs, tensor-parallel settings, GPU generations
measurement_method: simulation validated against measured power traces
caveat: Median across configurations; tail configurations exceed this.

quantity: Idle / static accelerator power under an agent loop
caveat: No retrieved source in this session reports a numeric idle or static accelerator power figure. elsworth2025google includes 'idle machine capacity' in its boundary and luo2026where attributes energy to 'tool-induced idle periods', but neither states a watt value in the retrieved text. MUST be sourced or declared an assumption.

quantity: Energy decomposition structure for LLM inference
value: fixed prefill + fixed generation setup + marginal per-step energy
unit: structural (J per request, J per step)
hardware_or_model: NVIDIA H100/H200, dense and MoE models
measurement_method: decomposed energy model fitted to measured request energy
caveat: This is the recommended structural form for a trajectory-level accounting model; the coefficients are hardware- and model-specific.

quantity: Throughput/cost gain from prefill-decode phase splitting
value: 1.4x throughput at 20% lower cost; or 2.35x throughput at equal cost and power
measurement_method: system evaluation of a phase-split cluster design
caveat: Cost and power budget are design-level, not per-request energy; does not directly give J/token.

quantity: Goodput gain from prefill/decode disaggregation
hardware_or_model: multiple LLMs and applications, SLO-constrained serving
caveat: >90% of requests within latency constraints; throughput, not energy. Energy gain must not be inferred 1:1.

quantity: Decode-specialised hardware: performance retained vs TDP saved
value: 97% of decode performance at 28% lower TDP
hardware_or_model: modelled H100 baseline vs proposed decode chips
caveat: Simulated against modelled H100s, not measured silicon. End-to-end: 19-41% lower hardware cost, 2-17% lower TDP.

quantity: MoE effect on fixed inference energy at low concurrency
hardware_or_model: MoE vs dense models on H100/H200
caveat: No single numeric factor given in the retrieved abstract; sparse routing and fragmented expert execution raise fixed energy at low concurrency.

quantity: Latency improvement from modular prefix/prompt cache reuse
hardware_or_model: GPU- and CPU-based inference, reused prompt modules
caveat: LATENCY, not energy, and first-token latency dominates the gain. Converting to energy saved requires an assumption about power during the saved interval.

quantity: End-to-end throughput gain from shared-prefix attention
hardware_or_model: CodeLlama-13B, large batch with shared prefix
caveat: Gain grows with batch size and shared-prefix length; the 32x figure is the best case, not typical.

quantity: Throughput degradation when shared prefix grows 1K to 16K tokens
caveat: Closest available proxy for a cache-reuse benefit curve; the session retrieved no source giving energy saved as a function of cache HIT RATE.

quantity: Compute saved as a function of KV/prefix-cache hit rate
unit: % compute saved per unit hit rate
caveat: No retrieved source states a hit-rate-to-compute-saved relation. KV-01..KV-03 are reuse-condition results, not hit-rate curves; modelling this requires an explicit assumption.

quantity: Energy saving from SLO-aware GPU frequency scaling
hardware_or_model: GPU inference serving under LLM inference traces
measurement_method: measured energy vs NVIDIA Triton baseline
caveat: Also reports >=1.71x energy-efficiency improvement under SLOs. Baseline is one specific serving stack.

quantity: Total energy reduction from correctly applied inference optimisations
hardware_or_model: multiple GPU architectures, software frameworks, decoding strategies, online and offline serving
measurement_method: empirical energy measurement across workload bins
caveat: 'Up to' figure; the paper's own finding is that effectiveness is highly sensitive to workload geometry, software stack and accelerator.

quantity: Energy reduction achievable with negligible user-experience impact
value: up to 70 (server scenario); up to 20 (batch scenario)
caveat: Server vs batch scenarios differ by 3.5x in achievable saving; scenario must be stated with the number.

quantity: Energy saved by kernel-level vs pass-level DVFS
caveat: TRAINING workload, not inference. Do not transfer the 14.6% to a decode-dominated agent trajectory without re-derivation.

quantity: Energy-efficiency improvement from GPU power-limit and batch-size optimisation
hardware_or_model: diverse DNN training workloads on GPUs
measurement_method: measured energy with an online optimiser
caveat: DNN training, pre-LLM-serving era; range is across workloads, not a confidence interval.

quantity: Carbon reduction from carbon-aware inference system design
hardware_or_model: AI inference cluster, cross-stack ILP design
caveat: Carbon, not energy; also reports offline batch inference at up to 55% of serving capacity, which is the lever being exploited.

quantity: End-to-end inference speedup from 4-bit post-training quantisation
hardware_or_model: OPT/BLOOM-class models on NVIDIA A100 and A6000
caveat: Speedup, not energy; the two GPU figures differ by 1.4x on identical software, so hardware must be stated.

quantity: Speedup and memory reduction from W8A8 post-training quantisation
caveat: Much smaller speedup than ME-01 at higher precision; quantisation speedup is not a single constant.

quantity: Speedup from activation-aware 4-bit weight quantisation
caveat: Baseline is an unoptimised FP16 reference implementation, which inflates the ratio relative to an optimised FP16 serving engine.

quantity: One-shot sparsity achievable with negligible perplexity increase
caveat: Sparsity is not energy: realising it as energy saved requires sparse kernel support, which the figure does not assume.

quantity: Inference acceleration from speculative decoding
caveat: Pre-LLM-serving-stack baseline; acceleration depends on draft-model acceptance rate, which is workload-dependent.

quantity: Model FLOPs utilisation achieved by optimised attention kernels
hardware_or_model: GPT-style model training on NVIDIA A100
caveat: TRAINING throughput; gives an upper reference for achievable accelerator utilisation, not an inference figure.

quantity: Cost reduction from LLM cascade at matched performance
hardware_or_model: GPT-4-class target, cascade of cheaper models
caveat: DOLLAR cost, not joules; API prices do not track provider energy (see liu2026energytotoken for the price-vs-cost caveat).

quantity: Reduction in self-consistency samples from early stopping
measurement_method: sample counting at comparable task performance
caveat: Benchmark-dependent by a factor of 2.5x; GSM8K -80.1%, StrategyQA -76.8%, CommonsenseQA -78.5%, Last Letters -67.4%. Sample count maps to energy only if per-sample energy is constant.

quantity: Efficiency gain from compute-optimal test-time scaling vs best-of-N
caveat: Also reports test-time compute outperforming a 14x larger model on problems where the small model has non-trivial success. FLOPs-matched, not joules-matched.

quantity: Benchmark size and best reported resolve rate, SWE-bench
value: 2294 problems; 1.96% resolved by best model at publication
hardware_or_model: 12 Python repositories; Claude 2 as best model at publication
caveat: Resolve rate is from the original 2023 evaluation and is now far out of date; do not quote as current agent capability.

quantity: Best agent vs human end-to-end task success, WebArena
caveat: 2023 figures; token and step counts per task are NOT reported in the retrieved abstract.

quantity: Best model vs human success, GAIA
caveat: 2023 figures; no per-task token or step counts in the retrieved abstract.

quantity: Number of distinct interactive environments, AgentBench
caveat: Structural figure only; the retrieved abstract reports no token or step counts per task.

quantity: Per-task token or step counts on standard agent benchmarks
measurement_method: empirical distributions of input length, output length and turn count derived from real agent traces
caveat: lau2026agentperfbench is the only retrieved source that explicitly samples empirical input-length, output-length and turn-count distributions from real agentic traces. The numeric distributions are not in the retrieved abstract and must be read from the paper.

quantity: Operator-reported fleet-average data-centre PUE
hardware_or_model: Amazon 1.15; Baidu 1.20; Google 1.09; Meta 1.08; Microsoft 1.16; Tencent 1.29
measurement_method: company sustainability reports (CY/FY 2024), compiled in Table 3 of the cited review
caveat: Self-reported, unaudited, and the reporting periods differ (Apple FY ended 2024-09-28, Microsoft FY ended 2024-06-30, Oracle CY 2023). Apple, Oracle and Tesla report no PUE. Values were read from a flattened text extraction of Table 3 - re-check against the published table before citing individual companies.

quantity: Operator-reported data-centre average WUE
measurement_method: company sustainability reports (CY/FY 2024), Table 3 of the cited review
caveat: Same caveats as PUE-01; a >10x spread across operators makes a single WUE constant indefensible.

quantity: Data centres as share of total company electricity consumption
measurement_method: operator-reported, ratio computed in the cited review
caveat: Only three of eleven surveyed companies report both figures; not generalisable.

quantity: Relative facility efficiency, cloud vs typical data centre
hardware_or_model: cloud data centres vs typical data centres
measurement_method: author estimate from published fleet data
caveat: Author estimate, 2021 vintage; overlaps conceptually with PUE but is not a PUE measurement.

quantity: Electricity-weighted average carbon intensity of US hyperscale data centre fleet
measurement_method: facility-level attributional model over EPA eGRID plant-level data
caveat: Attributional, location-based; explicitly ~48% ABOVE the national grid average, i.e. hyperscale siting is dirtier than average in this accounting. Does not reflect market-based (PPA/REC) claims.

quantity: US national grid-average carbon intensity (contemporaneous)
caveat: Average, not marginal. Pairing CI-01 and CI-02 is like-for-like; pairing either with a market-based figure is not.

quantity: US hyperscale fleet electricity consumption
caveat: Range is a scenario band over assumed facility load, not a measurement uncertainty interval. Corresponds to ~1.8% of US electricity in the central scenario; 54% of attributed generation fossil-fuelled.

quantity: Attributable CO2 of US hyperscale fleet
caveat: Scenario band, as CI-03.

quantity: Geographic variation in carbon-free energy fraction and resulting CO2e
hardware_or_model: cloud regions, within one country and one organisation
caveat: Underpins carbon-aware placement arguments; magnitude is dated (2021) and organisation-specific.

quantity: Marginal vs average carbon intensity signal choice
value: signal choice materially changes measured savings
caveat: No single numeric factor retrieved; cite alongside wiesner2025marginal, which argues marginal intensity is a poor metric for both carbon accounting and grid signalling. Average and marginal figures must never be mixed in one budget.

quantity: ML accelerator effectiveness vs off-the-shelf systems
caveat: Combined with datacentre and model choice the paper claims up to ~100-1000x total footprint reduction - a compounded best case, not an expected value.

quantity: Generational improvement in carbon-per-compute for TPUs
unit: x improvement (TPU v4i to TPU v6e)
caveat: LCA-based; embodied and operational contributions are combined in the reported 'CCI' metric.

quantity: Training footprint of a 176B model: operational vs full life cycle
hardware_or_model: BLOOM-176B training on a known cluster
measurement_method: bottom-up estimate from measured power and energy-mix data
caveat: The 2.0x gap between boundaries is the clearest published demonstration that the accounting boundary dominates the reported number.

quantity: Projected growth in AI electricity use to 2030, high-adoption scenario
measurement_method: scenario model over usage growth, hardware efficiency and IPCC electricity-mix scenarios
caveat: Scenario, not forecast; the high-adoption scenario is explicitly driven by generative AI AND agent adoption, which makes it the most relevant projection for this paper.

quantity: Energy consumption of large generative models vs traditional models
caveat: 'Up to' comparison across model classes; task is not held constant.

quantity: Projected AI carbon and water footprint, 2025
measurement_method: approximation of AI workloads via data-centre general performance metrics
caveat: Authors state the AI/non-AI workload split cannot be resolved from current disclosure; the range reflects that, not measurement error.

quantity: Projected global AI water withdrawal, 2027
caveat: Withdrawal, not consumption; the two are routinely conflated.

quantity: Inference share of total AI power consumption
measurement_method: cited industry reports, restated by the authors
caveat: Secondhand claim attributed to unnamed industry reports in the retrieved abstract. Trace to the primary source before using.

quantity: Growth in compute used by deep-learning research, 2012-2018
measurement_method: cited third-party analysis, restated by the authors
caveat: Secondhand and now historical; cite for framing only.

quantity: AI data-centre share of global electricity demand
measurement_method: not established - value read from the retrieved record TITLE only
caveat: The abstract was NOT retrieved in this session; only the title and bibliographic record were verified. Do not cite this number until the source is read.
